title: POC weekly sync - quality eval (Harbor Pharma)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results on the pilot prompt set. Discussed recent regression on dosage-extraction prompts after switching to 4-bit quantized variant, prompt-tuning adjustments, guardrails for hallucination, and next steps: new eval run, updated prompt set, security docs share, and performance deep-dive scheduling.
action_items: Anika Bose - Share ground-truth spreadsheet for dosage-extraction prompts - due 2026-08-24
Diego Ramos - Re-run eval with latest 4-bit quantized model and include token-level diff stats - due 2026-08-22
Maya Patel - Send updated prompt set (v1.1) and eval rubric to the team - due 2026-08-20
Tom Wallace - Share access to staging VPC endpoints and logs for the last 48 hours - due 2026-08-21
Lina Ho - Compile security checklist and SOC2 docs link for Harbor review - due 2026-08-23
next_steps: Redwood to run targeted regression tests on dosage/extraction prompts
Customer to validate ground-truth labels and flag ambiguous cases
Decision on quantized vs unquantized model for stage rollout by end of week
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-19 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), Anika (Harbor ML), Tom (Harbor Platform), Ethan (Harbor Research), Maya J. (PM)

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we only have 45 minutes so we'll focus on the quality evals from last run. quick recap - we deployed the 4-bit quantized variant to staging last tuesday and ran the prompt set across 3k cases.
00:22 Anika: hi, yeah thanks. overall we saw a drop in exact-extraction on the dosage prompts, about 6% down, which is higher than we'd expect for quantization. some of it feels like tokenization boundary issues.
00:38 Diego: yep, we noticed that too. looks like the model sometimes splits units (mg) into separate tokens which affects regex post-proc, also KV cache warmup seemed different under continuous batching.
00:55 Ethan: could be the compiler/kernel selection change you mentioned, Diego, the tiny kernels for 4-bit run different attention numerics.
01:10 Maya: right, so quick question - is this a quality regression we can fix with prompt edits or do we need to move off 4-bit for now?
01:25 Anika: leaning towards prompt fixes first; if we can tighten the expected output shape and add an explicit anchor token for dosage, maybe we recover. but we want the eval run to prove it.
01:40 Diego: action here is re-run eval with prompt v1.1 that forces a single-line "dosage: <value>" pattern and include token-level diffs. I'll also capture the tokenization boundary stats.
01:55 Tom: for context our downstream parser relies on exact match, so small token splits break pipelines. we can relax parser but prefer model output consistency.
02:12 Maya: understood. on the safety/guardrails side - any new hits? hallucination frequency?
02:25 Anika: hallucination rate is low overall, but a few free-text summary prompts invented measurements for older drugs. those are lower priority but we flagged them.
02:40 Lina: note that some of the transcripts in the run show slightly different model names in logs e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" in one header, that's from noisy instrumentation.
02:55 Diego: ha, our bad, logger mapping mismatch. we'll normalize.
03:10 Ethan: about scoring rubric - can we include weighted metrics? exact-extract (0.6), semantic-accuracy (0.3), safe-output (0.1) - that reflects our priorities.
03:30 Maya: yes we can. we'll add that weighting and re-compute the composite score. current composite dropped from 0.92 to 0.86 on the quant run.
03:48 Anika: can you show an example failing case?
04:02 Diego: sure, failing example 1: prompt id 1423. expected "dosage: 50 mg" got "dosage: 50" + newline then "mg" on next token. regex failed.
04:25 Maya J.: this is where a small post-process sanitizer might help but we prefer model to output canonical unit.
04:40 Maya: agreed - prefer model fix first. also, any latency impact? we saw tail latency increase by ~12% in bursty scenarios.
04:56 Diego: that's likely due to continuous batching interacting with KV cache miss patterns on the new kernel. we need to run perf traces.
05:10 Tom: i'll give you staging logs; we'll check concurrency config.
05:22 Maya: on guardrails - do we have a quick hallucination detector? Diego: we have a basic scoring filter that flags low-confidence tokens based on logprobs, but it's noisy. we can add entailment checks or use a secondary verifier model.
05:44 Anika: verifier sounds good but increases cost; want Redwood recommendations on cost/benefit.
06:00 Maya: will include that in the next write-up.
06:12 Ethan: also want to ensure audit logs show token-level diffs for regulatory review.
06:22 Lina: Redwood Console can surface per-route token breakdowns, we'll enable retention for the evaluation route and share dashboard link.
06:35 Anika: perfect. one other ask - can we pin model versions for the pilot? we don't want auto-rollouts to change behavior mid-eval.
06:48 Diego: yes, Dedicated/Private customers can pin; for hosted we can set rollout policy. we'll pin the quant variant to the staging route for the next 72 hours.
07:05 Maya J.: timeline question - what's the earliest we can run a follow-up eval?
07:15 Diego: if we get the v1.1 prompt set today, i can re-run overnight and have results by tomorrow EOD.
07:25 Anika: we'll send prompt edits after this call.
07:32 Maya: ok let's capture concrete next steps - re-run eval with v1.1, share ground truth, perf deep-dive next week, security docs share.
07:44 Tom: quick procurement note - we're evaluating cost per 1k tokens, does Redwood have updated pricing for quantized models?
07:55 Maya: yes, we have a quant pricing sheet, i'll share. quantized typically reduces token compute cost but may have perf tradeoffs.
08:10 Anika: competitor note: we compared a small run on Anthropic and saw similar token-splitting; might be model-tokenizer combo rather than vendor.
08:30 Maya: good datapoint.
08:40 Diego: any blockers on our side? we'll need access to staging endpoints + the GT spreadsheet.
08:50 Tom: i'll send the VPC access and logs by tomorrow.
09:00 Maya: great. final recap: Maya to send prompt v1.1 + pricing + security link; Diego to re-run eval and share token-diff report; Anika to send GT labels. Lina to collect docs.
09:18 Anika: thanks everyone.
09:25 Maya: thanks, end call.
